newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea's Kim promotes six army officers.
newsitem.headline: North Korea's Kim promotes six army officers.

text.p: North Korea's de facto leader Kim Jong-il has announced the promotion of six relatively young army officers close to him, a move analysts said indicated he could be consolidating his power base.
In a dispatch on Monday monitored in Tokyo, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said Kim Jong-il described the soldiers as "leading officers" of the Korean People's Army.
Those promoted to army generals were Kim Kyok-sik, Ju Sang-song, Kim Song-gyu and Pak Jae-gyong, KCNA said.
Ri Chang-hwan and Pak Yong-ha were promoted to lieutenant-generals, KCNA said.

Tokyo-based North Korea analyst Noriyuki Suzuki of Radiopress news service said all six officers were in their fifties, relatively young for senior army officers in a military whose leaders are nearly all in their seventies and eighties.
Suzuki said North Korea's official media had regularly reported that the six were at Kim's side during his visits to military units over the past two years.
"The fact that Secretary Kim Jong-il was able to pick and promote these young men means that he is functioning well as supreme commander of the Korean People's Army," Suzuki said.
"It could also mean that Kim Jong-il is consolidating his power base," he added.

"It (Kim's promotion order) expressed the firm belief that they (the six officers) would as ever uphold the party and the leader with loyalty and filial piety, further strengthen the people's army and reliably defend the Juche (self-reliance) revolutionary cause by arms," KCNA said.

Kim Jong-il, 54, supreme commander of the country's 1.1-million-strong military, has yet to be formally confirmed in two key posts held by his late father Kim Il-sung -- general secretary of the ruling Workers' Party and state president.
Korea watchers believe Kim Jong-il is likely to formally assume the posts this July, on the third anniversary of his father's death.
